title: A Reductions Approach to Fair Classification
authors: Alekh Agarwal, Alina Beygelzimer, Miroslav Dudík, John Langford, Hanna Wallach
venue: Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR vol. 80, pp. 60-69
conclusions: Reduces fair binary classification under demographic parity (DP) or equalized odds (EO) to a sequence of cost-sensitive classification problems, treating the base classifier as a black box.

Formulates fairness as linear constraints on conditional moments (Mu(h) <= c) and solves the resulting Lagrangian saddle point via an exponentiated-gradient no-regret scheme (Algorithm 1) that iteratively updates Lagrange multipliers lambda over the constraints.

Returns a randomized classifier that is provably near the lowest-error classifier subject to the fairness constraints, with finite-sample statistical guarantees (Theorems 1-3) as a function of Rademacher complexity.
Requires training-time access to the protected attribute but NOT test-time access, unlike post-processing methods (e.g., Hardt et al. 2016) that need the protected attribute at test time.

Empirically shown on four datasets (adult income, COMPAS, Law School, Dutch census) to dominate or match baselines (unconstrained, post-processing, reweighting, relabeling) on the accuracy-fairness tradeoff.
Also proposes a grid-search variant for low-dimensional (binary) protected attributes as an alternative to the full exponentiated-gradient search.
our_use: main.tex ~line 170: '...group-wise constraints underpin fair classification \citep{zafar2017fairness,agarwal2018reductions}, the trained analogues of our local caps.' -- cited alongside Zafar et al. as canonical training-time, group-wise (Lagrangian/dual) fairness-constraint methods that our per-group local caps are analogous to.
